text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: pgsql-conn-threshold fired for service 'redwood-db-prod' (High). Trigger: pg.max_connections > 95% on primary-us-west2. Alert URL: https://pagerduty.local/INC12345

Sam H: Acked. I’m on call and taking ownership. tagging @Maria G for DB diagnostics.

Maria G: On it. Looking at pgbouncer stats and the app connection graphs. Initial glance: pgbouncer avg-clients ~ 1020 (max configured 1024), pool queue spiking to ~800, accept queue growing. Also seeing a correlated spike in redis-client TIMEOUTs in the same region.

Kevin L: Is this a traffic spike from external customers or an internal job?

Maria G: Seems multi-source. Top talker by IP shows traffic from a set of hostnames matching our real-time-indexer batch job. I’m pulling logs now.

opsbot: Runbook for pgsql-conn-threshold (short id: DB-POOL-01) 
1) Reduce incoming connection rate (edge rate-limit).
2) Scale pgbouncer pool size or enable overflow to read-replicas.
3) Temp-enable read-only fallback for non-critical routes.
4) Investigate upstream caller for flood.

Sam H: Ok step 1: can someone apply an emergency rate-limit on the HTTP edge for user-facing write routes (route: /v1/generate, /v1/complete)? Use 429 for short period. @Jen C can you patch the edge?

Jen C: On it. Pushing a quick rule to the WAF and edge-router:
```
# emergency rule
route: /v1/generate
limit: 30rps per-ip
response: 429
ttl: 300s
```
Pushed to us-west2 in 30s.

Maria G: While that rolls, I’m going to increase pgbouncer max_client_conn on the primary from 1024 -> 2048 and drain idle clients. Doing it in a staged fashion (apply to the pool on one host then roll). Running:
```
sudo -u postgres psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 2000;"
systemctl restart postgresql
# pgbouncer config change
sed -i 's/max_client_conn = 1024/max_client_conn = 2048/' /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
systemctl reload pgbouncer
```
Note: doing reload to avoid full drop.

Kevin L: Heads-up that raising max_connections will increase memory. Maria make sure we have headroom on those hosts.

Maria G: Confirmed current free mem ~ 6GB on each primary. Increasing to 2048 should be safe for short window. Watching for OOM.

Sam H: Parallel task: can we divert non-critical traffic to read-replicas (read-only) and turn on connection pooling at app layer? That reduces write traffic hitting primary.

Maria G: I can promote a replica routing rule for select API keys. Applying canary: route 10% of read queries to replica pool.

Jen C: Edge limits are live — seeing a drop in incoming RPS to the write endpoints. 5xx rate down from 8% -> 3% already.

pagerduty-bot: Alert update: incident acknowledged by Sam H. Escalation schedule paused.

Maria G: After pgbouncer reload, queue length dropping from ~800 -> ~120 on the first host. Second host in roll now. Redis TIMEOUTs still present but less frequent.

Kevin L: What about the redis evictions you mentioned? Could that be making app retry hot and amplify connections?

Maria G: Yes suspicious. Redis memory spikes coincide with the indexer job writing lots of ephemeral keys. Eviction samples show LRU churn and latency 50-150ms during peak. I can temporarily change eviction policy to volatile-lru and increase maxmemory on cache nodes by 2GB by resizing the VM group.

Sam H: Do it. Also throttle the indexer job if possible. Who owns that?

Kevin L: I can reach out to the infra team owning indexer, but can we also block the indexer CID range at the edge as a quick throttle?

Jen C: I can add a CIDR-level limit. Which prefix? Maria/ Kevin provide the netblock.

Maria G: Indexer hosts: 10.12.48.0/24 (internal). Kevin, please confirm you want that limited.

Kevin L: Confirmed. Please limit to 5rps per-host. Jen do it.

Jen C: Done. Edge shows significantly reduced write burst. App retries dropping.

opsbot: Actions in progress: [edge-rule applied], [pgbouncer scale started], [redis mem bump queued], [indexing CIDR throttled].

Maria G: Redis mem bump completed on cache-02 and cache-03. Eviction rate down to normal. No immediate OOMs. pgbouncer roll completed across primaries, queue length stabilized under 50.

Sam H: Good. Next verify user-visible impact and customer routes. Any erroring customers? Support?

Kevin L: Support reports a handful of customers saw increased latency and a few transient errors during peak. I’m opening a short PSA and will follow-up with CS.

Maria G: Logs indicate write transactions that hit primary during the peak had higher lock wait times ~400-600ms, but no transaction failures at DB level. Most client-side failures were timeouts at API layer.

Sam H: TL;DR: root cause appears to be internal indexing job unexpectedly ramping traffic causing Redis evictions -> app retries -> connection fanout to Postgres -> pgbouncer queueing. Mitigations: edge rate limits, CIDR throttle for indexer, pgbouncer scale, redis memory increase. Monitoring: keep for 2 hours.

Jen C: Rolling back emergency edge rule in 10m as we let queued traffic drain, unless you want it longer.

Sam H: Keep for 30m. We’ll do a controlled rollback when metrics stable.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status changed to 'stabilized' (no critical alerts firing). Auto-escalation re-enabled.

Maria G: I’ll follow up with a short post-incident note and include metrics: pgbouncer queue peak 820 -> stable < 50, redis eviction/sec peak 120 -> <5, API 5xx peak 8% -> 0.6%.

Kevin L: I’ll coordinate with infra to add a pre-flight check on the indexer job to prevent unbounded ramp. Also proposing a guard: if redis eviction/sec > 50 then indexer pauses automatically.

Sam H: Thanks everyone. I’m closing the on-call handoff in 45m unless anything else flares. @pagerduty-bot tag me if any followups. :thumbsup:
